concept.title: A bounded academic decision
concept.audienceGap: The student assumes more visual decoration will satisfy a task marked on reasoning.
concept.hlni: The requested output and its marking criterion are different; the criterion can change preparation.
concept.viewerChange: Replace a broad degree-fit worry with a question about the observed difficulty.
concept.concept: A hypothetical poster criterion requires explaining one design choice; the student changes their preparation.
concept.device: A crossed-out decoration plan is replaced with a reason.
concept.support: The observation identifies one missing answer; it does not predict aptitude or success.
methodSteps: Mark the precise uncertainty and ask about that uncertainty.
concept.interpretationRule: A task-specific question is justified; a degree-fit conclusion is not.
concept.visibleProof: The student writes the uncertainty next to the actual item and uses it to ask for help.
concept.payoff: The student feels better after hearing the advice.
concept.limitations: One activity does not establish degree suitability, curriculum membership or aptitude.

demonstration.input: A hypothetical poster assignment supplies the marking criterion: explain one design choice.
demonstration.visibleInput: Example criterion: explain one design choice.
demonstration.observation: Decorating another slide would not supply the required explanation.
demonstration.nextQuestion: Which reason supports my design choice?

storySpine.startingBelief: Adding decoration will satisfy the hypothetical assignment.
storySpine.studentSituation: A student plans work after assuming degree labels identify assessment demands.
storySpine.observation: The supplied illustrative criterion rewards explaining a design choice.
storySpine.focus: Preparing an explanation rather than additional decoration
storySpine.whyQuestionFollows: Choosing a reason directly addresses the known explanatory criterion.
storySpine.changedAction: The student feels confident about choosing a degree.
storySpine.visibleConsequence: The student smiles, closes the notebook, and feels calm.
storySpine.channelExperience: An explanatory demonstration reveals how a criterion changes preparation.

demonstration.input: A hypothetical school-event expense list has a refundable deposit with no category supplied.
demonstration.observation: The student cannot classify the refundable deposit.
demonstration.nextQuestion: How should I classify this refundable deposit, and why?

storySpine.startingBelief: My difficulty means I should copy my friend’s degree choice.
storySpine.studentSituation: Two friends considering B.Com and BBA inspect a hypothetical event expense list.
storySpine.observation: The refundable deposit has no category stated in the sample.
storySpine.whyQuestionFollows: The missing category is exactly what the student asks to understand.
storySpine.changedAction: The student stops copying a degree choice and asks a teacher about the deposit.
storySpine.visibleConsequence: The student circles the deposit and writes the matching question beside it for the teacher.
storySpine.channelExperience: A friend helps turn an anxious self-judgement into a precise help request.

concept.title: A bounded academic decision
concept.audienceGap: Students make broad degree judgements from a single difficulty.
concept.hlni: Business Simulation appears in both of the supplied Semester I programme lists.
concept.viewerChange: Replace a broad degree-fit worry with a question about the observed difficulty.
concept.concept: A student tests the claim that these two title lists are completely separate by comparing the inspected official rows.
concept.device: One highlighted row in each scoped official document changes the comparison shortlist.
concept.support: The supplied official B.Com PDF p.5 and BBA Entrepreneurship Management PDF p.9 list this title; the claim is limited to these inspected rows.
methodSteps: Mark the precise uncertainty and ask about that uncertainty.
concept.interpretationRule: A task-specific question is justified; a degree-fit conclusion is not.
concept.visibleProof: The student writes the uncertainty next to the actual item and uses it to ask for help.
concept.payoff: A global worry is replaced by a specific request that can be answered.
concept.limitations: This establishes the shared title in these two published documents only, not identical content, current admissions or degree suitability.

demonstration.input: The two supplied official Semester I rows, with exact programme names and document cohort visible.
demonstration.visibleInput: Business Organization & Management — both scoped Semester I lists
demonstration.observation: Both inspected rows list Business Simulation.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What teaching and assessment does each actual programme specify?

storySpine.startingBelief: These two programmes cannot share a course title.
storySpine.studentSituation: A student has rejected one programme because of the degree label.
storySpine.observation: Business Simulation is shared in the supplied documents.
storySpine.focus: Title overlap versus the separate question of course depth
storySpine.whyQuestionFollows: Shared titles refute complete title separation but do not establish identical teaching.
storySpine.changedAction: The student restores the rejected programme to the shortlist and requests the actual course briefs.
storySpine.visibleConsequence: Both exact programme names and the 2025–26 scope remain visible as the student adds an assessment-brief-needed column.
storySpine.channelExperience: A curiosity-led assumption is corrected by scoped official evidence.
